originality.rationale: The exact perfect-square dual-rate global optimum and its collapse under chiral reversal do not follow as stated from the inspected closest works: deterministic stroboscopic restarts, measurement-only conditional resetting, two-level random probing, fixed-time magnetic rings, and continuous sinks use different controls or dynamics. Published-record semantic searches and a direct comparison with the full available source/result texts found no equivalent theorem. A more general unindexed spectral/renewal formula might subsume this specialization, and scientific priority is qualified.
residual_risks: Quantum restart papers have established competing/discontinuous optima in other control variables; this finding does not assert those broad phenomena are new.
A more general unindexed renewal probing or three-level spectral calculation could imply the exact special case despite no located statement.
The exact tie is a special ideal Hamiltonian and may split under perturbations or resetting overhead, so experimental robustness is not established.
No independent literature-priority evaluation or scientific audit has been performed.

value.rationale: A sharp exact nonunique positive optimum for a single mean quantum search time, together with its collapse to a unique optimum under magnetic reversal, is a physically motivated phase-sensitive limitation on probe-rate design. The exact algebraic tie is not a routine restatement of known single-rate two-level optimization nor a numerical coincidence. Assumed perfect re-preparation makes this a model-specific exact result, not a claim of hardware robustness.
